title: After-Dark Escalation Playbook — Annotations and Handoff
body:
Quick summary (overnight watch)
- Date: 2027-09-14, shift: 00:00-08:00 PT
- Primary owner for shift: Asha Patel (on-call)
- Incident window: 2027-09-14 01:17 — 2027-09-14 02:26 PT (stabilized, ongoing follow-ups)
- Customer impact: Elevated gen latency + 5xx rate for Hosted API region-eu-west-1 for ~65 minutes at peak. No data leak, no auth failures observed.

Timeline (high level)
- 01:17 — Pager alert: hosted-api-req-500-rate > 2% for 5m (alert: api-errors-high).
- 01:19 — Preliminary triage (logs + traces): error pattern consistent with upstream kv-cache timeouts and a couple kv-retry storms.
- 01:23 — Escalated to serving-runtime on-call (Jamal); started SRE bridge.
- 01:30 — Temporary routing rule applied: route ~12% traffic to standby-serving-pool in eu-west-1a (traffic-split via routing policy).
- 01:38 — Observed partial recovery in error rate but latency remained elevated for long tails.
- 01:50 — Attempted cache-pool scale-up (manual) + increased request timeout from 4s -> 6s for model-gen route (short-term mitigation).
- 02:06 — Found one node with NVMe saturation and I/O wait spikes (instance id: rwi-gpu-34-eu). Removed node from pool and cordoned.
- 02:18 — Error rate returned to baseline; latency slowly recovering.
- 02:26 — Declared incident contained; bridge handed over to morning ops with follow-up tasks.

Symptoms observed
- 5xx surge (502/504 variants) on model-gen endpoints for specific model variants with long prefixes.
- KV cache timeouts (redis-like) and repeated retries amplified backend load.
- NVMe I/O wait on a serving node correlated with high KV latency from that node.
- Trace samples show long tail at step: kv-fetch -> model-decode -> response-queue.

Immediate mitigations executed (and why)
- Traffic split to standby-serving-pool: reduce load on suspect pool while preserving throughput. Implemented because autoscaler was caught up and manual splitting is fastest.
- Increased request timeout for model-gen: prevented client-side cancellations and reduced retry storms.
- Cordoned & drained rwi-gpu-34-eu: node exhibited NVMe saturation, removing it reduced KV contention and I/O wait.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive KV client retry (sdk-config override) to avoid cascading retries.

Runbook steps used (notes on gaps)
- Referenced: Confluence -> After-Dark Escalation Playbook (linked above).
- Runbook step 'isolate-suspect-node' works but lacks guidance for NVMe-specific checks — we added a short checklist below.
- 'reduce-retry-behavior' step helped but runbook doesn't indicate which config keys to patch for older model-runtime versions (we patched runtime.cfg kv.max_retries=false). Add exact keys.

Commands and diagnostics (copied from shell notes)
- kubectl -n hosting get pods -l pool=eu-west-1a -o wide  # checked pod distribution
- tailscale ssh rwi-gpu-34-eu  # debug access (used internal bastion)
- iostat -x 2 10  # confirmed nvme io wait spikes
- curl -s "https://observability/metrics?m=kv.latency.percentile.99&range=1h" | jq .
- /opt/runtime/bin/config-override --set kv.client.retries=0 --service model-gen

What deviated from runbook (actionable)
- Runbook assumes autoscaler will reduce load; our autoscaler config has a 5m cooldown and didn’t react fast enough. Need tuning for cache-thrashing scenarios.
- No explicit NVMe checklist (SMART, fio, kernel logs) in runbook — add to 'isolate-suspect-node' step.
- Playbook suggests switching to fallback models; we avoided automatic fallback because variant pinning would drop quality for customers — clarify tradeoffs in doc.

Follow-ups / tickets created (owners + ETA)
- SRE-5821: Add NVMe diagnostic checklist to runbook + include exact iostat/fio sample commands (owner: Kaito, ETA: 2027-09-20).
- SRE-5822: Autoscaler cooldown tuning for cache-backed serving pools (owner: Jamal, ETA: 2027-09-18).
- SRE-5823: Patch runtime config docs with precise keys for retry behavior across runtime versions (owner: Marta, ETA: 2027-09-19).
- INC-2134: Incident record & timeline (owner: Asha, ETA: 2027-09-16) — link above.

Metrics snapshot (peak)
- 5xx rate: 2.7% (alert threshold 2.0%) at 01:25
- p95 latency: 1.9s -> p99: 6.2s (normal p99 ~ 1.1s)
- KV p99 latency: 420ms -> 1.8s during peak
- CPU on rwi-gpu-34-eu: ~36% but iowait spiked to 48%

Runbook additions I propose (short bullets)
- NVMe diagnostic checklist + sample commands and acceptable thresholds.
- Explicit guidance on when to apply traffic split vs fallback model routing (decision tree).
- Quick rollback snippets for runtime config keys (how to revert override).
- Add 'disable-app-level-retries' as an explicit mitigation for cache-thrashing incidents.
- Alarm tuning: add a p99-kv-latency alert with lower noise threshold for cache-backed pools.

Handoff notes for morning ops (what to check first)
- Verify rwi-gpu-34-eu remains cordoned and is scheduled for hardware/host investigation (SRE-5821).
- Confirm autoscaler tuning patch is staged (SRE-5822) or at least understand current cooldown window.
- Validate no residual client retry spike by checking gateway retry-meter and error-rate correlation.
- Keep incident tag INC-2134 open until all follow-ups complete.

Loose questions / hypotheses for postmortem
- Were the NVMe spikes a symptom (e.g., OS-level GC, snapshotting, or preemptible maintenance) or cause? Need host-level logs and provider activity.
- Did a recent model rollout change I/O pattern (larger KV fetches)? Correlate deploy windows.
- Is our KV client backoff policy aggressive enough when upstream latency increases?

Minutes for next retro (proposed agenda)
- 10m: Timeline + impact recap (Asha)
- 15m: Technical root-cause hypotheses + host diagnostics (Kaito)
- 15m: Runbook gaps + action assignment (Jamal)
- 10m: Alerting & SLO implications (Product SRE rep)
- 10m: Open Q&A and confirm owners/ETAs

Appendix: quick NVMe checklist (to add to runbook)
- iostat -x 1 10 => look for %iowait > 30% sustained
- dmesg | tail -n 200 => look for nvme errors, driver resets
- sudo fio --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4 --runtime=30 --time_based
- smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1  # if supported by host; record SMART attributes
- Check provider maintenance logs if node is preemptible

Notes to next on-call:
- Slack thread: #eng-sre (search "INC-2134") has live traces and screenshots — use them for quick context.
- If you re-enable traffic to the drained pool, do it gradually (10% -> 30% -> 50% over 10m) and watch kv.p99 and api.5xx closely.
- I left a small snippet in the runtime config repo with the override we applied (see PR link). Revert instructions are in the PR description.

Signed-off-by: Asha Patel (on-call)
_notes: Informal night-shift handoff doc. Draft status because follow-ups may update timeline.
